records.name: Spruce Street Minyan
records.summary: An egalitarian prayer group for Jewish people in their 20s and 30s who live in Philadelphia. It holds a monthly Friday night service followed by a shared Shabbat meal.
records.what_you_do: Come to the monthly Friday night service and stay for the Shabbat meal, sign up to volunteer, or email the group to introduce yourself.

schedule.text: A Friday evening service once a month, followed by a Shabbat meal. RSVP on OneTable is required for each service.

cost.text: The site lists no ticket price, meal cost or suggested donation.

first_step.how: RSVP on OneTable for the next monthly service, or email the group to introduce yourself first
first_step.basis: The services are public and have a clear RSVP route and an email address. The site does not say newcomers are welcomed by name, and it has no separate page for new people.
first_step.what_to_expect: The service is held on a Friday evening once a month, and a shared Shabbat meal follows. The site does not say how long the service runs, so email the group with questions before you come. The group is aimed at Jewish people in their 20s and 30s, including young professionals and graduate students.
first_visit_tips: RSVP on OneTable before you come, since the site says RSVP is required.
Email the group to ask for the address, because the site names only a community space in Philadelphia.
Plan to stay for the Shabbat meal, which the site presents as part of the evening.

records.notes: Only the home page could be read. The upcoming events page and the contact page were not found at the addresses tried (404). The home page lists two services, October 16, 2026 and November 13, 2026, with RSVP for the first; these are kept out of schedule text. A niggun circle is listed for Sunday, October 18 with no year, so it was not recorded. The word egalitarian comes from tier 1 and was not repeated on the pages read, so it was kept. The footer year is a copyright line and was not used as evidence. No street address is published, so no location is recorded.

records.name: SquashSmarts
records.summary: A program that pairs squash with fitness training, school help, leadership work and long-term mentoring. It is based at the Lenfest Center in North Philadelphia.
records.what_you_do: Young players take part in squash, fitness, academic support and leadership work. Adults can volunteer as tutors or squash coaches on weekday afternoons once their clearances are done, or join the Young Friends Network, a group of college students and young professionals who mentor and help out.

schedule.text: Tutoring and squash coaching happen on weekday afternoons, most often 4 to 6 pm during practice hours, with times worked out one on one. The site does not publish a student practice schedule.

locations.label: Arlen Specter US Squash Center (SquashSmarts West Philadelphia)

cost.text: The site does not state a program fee. It names two scholarships, the Clif Wright and Carols Kids scholarships, without amounts or eligibility rules.

first_step.how: Call 215-221-6860 to ask how a young player enrolls. To volunteer as a tutor or coach, fill in the volunteer form and finish the clearances first.
first_step.basis: The site gives a phone line for questions but does not describe how a new player or family joins. Volunteers need a form, three clearances and a shift sign up before they can start.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteer tutors and coaches work with young players most weekday afternoons, from 4 to 6 pm, and the schedule is set one on one. Before a first shift you need a child abuse clearance, a State Police check and an FBI check, and the site says these last five years. The site does not describe what a family does on a first visit, so ask by phone first.
first_visit_tips: Start the clearances early, since they must be finished before you can volunteer.
Call 215-221-6860 before you go, because the site does not describe enrollment steps.
Plan around weekday afternoons, when most tutoring and coaching happens.

access.notes: The contact page names the Broad Street Line, Erie Avenue stop, and the 53 bus from Broad and Erie to the Lenfest Center. The West Philadelphia site is reached from the Market Frankford Line at 34th Street, with a trolley connection to 33rd Street, and visitors check in at the front desk.

records.notes: The site gives no student enrollment steps, practice schedule or fee, so the first step is a phone call. Squash has no tag of its own in the vocabulary, so tennis_pickleball is the closest racquet tag. The clearances (child abuse, State Police and FBI) are listed for tutors and coaches; the page says nothing about clearances for students, so requirements are recorded for volunteers. The email address on the contact page is hidden behind a spam filter and was not recorded. The Young Friends page describes optional gifts of 5 or 10 dollars a month, or 50 or 100 dollars once, and these are contributions, not fees, so they are not in cost. Other volunteer roles on the volunteer page: group projects for companies and teams, a spring cleanup, and an April fundraiser, both with sign up coming soon. Two dated events on the home page are not in schedule text: a Phillies night on September 22, 2026 (the last sign of life) and a U.S. Open squash night on November 2, 2026.

records.name: St. Agatha-St. James Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish at 38th and Chestnut streets that serves students and young adults through the Newman Center on its campus. It offers Mass, adult and young adult groups, Bible studies and a homeless outreach team.
records.what_you_do: Come to Sunday or weekday Mass, join the Wednesday young adults and grad students group, take a FOCUS Bible study, or sign up for the homeless outreach team or other service. Adults over 16 who want to become Catholic can join the OCIA program, which meets on Tuesday evenings from 6 to 8 pm.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 9 am, 11:30 am and 5:30 pm. Weekday Mass in the Newman Chapel at 12:05 pm, plus 5:30 pm Tuesday to Friday during the school year. The young adults and grad students group meets every Wednesday at 6:30 pm, and OCIA classes meet on Tuesdays from 6 to 8 pm during the 2026 to 2027 year.

locations.label: Main church and Newman Center
locations.address: 38th and Chestnut Sts. (parish office at 111 South 38th St., 3rd floor)

cost.text: Mass is free to attend. The site does not list a fee for its groups, and parish membership has no dues.

first_step.how: Come to a Sunday Mass, then join the Wednesday 6:30 pm young adults and grad students group at the Newman Center, 111 South 38th Street.
first_step.basis: The site has a page for new parishioners with an email list and no dues, a phone line for questions, a weekly young adult group open to all, and an adult initiation program for people still deciding. The full steps on the new parishioner page were not readable, so the rating rests on these named routes.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone, with Sunday Masses at 9 am, 11:30 am and 5:30 pm. The young adults and grad students group meets each Wednesday at 6:30 pm at the Newman Center, where the site says members grow in faith and serve others together. The page does not say whether you need to register before you attend, so ask the group's contact at your first visit.
first_visit_tips: If you want the young adult group, come on a Wednesday at 6:30 pm.
Sign up for the parish email list if you want news; the form asks for a permanent mailing address, not a dorm address.
The Newman Center and the parish office both use the 111 South 38th Street address, and the church is at 38th and Chestnut.
Call the parish office at 267-787-5000 if you have questions about groups before you come.

records.notes: The Newman Center at 111 South 38th Street hosts the young adult group. The Penn and Drexel Newman small group pages describe the same Newman groups: a Latino small group on Tuesdays at 8 pm, an athletes group on Thursdays at 8 pm, a FOCUS Bible study, and a Filipino group that meets on first Saturdays with a 7 pm Mass. These are parish-run groups, not recorded separately, and a later pass could take them. Staff email addresses on those pages and on the OCIA page were not recorded. The OCIA page shows one email address but links to a different one, so only the Google form and the phone line are given. Status moved from probably_active to active on the 2026 to 2027 OCIA schedule. The Penn and Drexel small group pages were read only for the group details and are not separate leads. The new parishioner page's detailed steps did not come through in the page read.

records.name: St. Athanasius Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish at Limekiln Pike and Walnut Lane that shares Sunday worship with St. Benedict Church. It offers Eucharistic adoration on Tuesdays, an online faith formation library that the parish pays for, and a food pantry listed under the St. Benedict name.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass: Saturday at 4 pm, Sunday at 8 am at St. Benedict Church or at 10 am here. Join the Wednesday Bible study or the Thursday Legion of Mary, both on Zoom at 7 pm. Use the St. Benedict food pantry on Monday or Friday from 10 to 11:30 am. Sign up for the FORMED library, which the parish pays for.

schedule.text: Saturday vigil Mass at 4 pm. Sunday Masses at 8 am (St. Benedict Church) and 10 am (St. Athanasius). Weekday Mass Monday to Friday at 9 am, livestreamed on YouTube. Adoration on Tuesdays from 9 am to 6:30 pm. Food pantry on Mondays and Fridays from 10 to 11:30 am at St. Benedict Church. Bible study on Wednesdays and Legion of Mary on Thursdays, both at 7 pm on Zoom. St. Vincent Society meets twice a month on Sundays at noon.

locations.label: Parish church
locations.address: Limekiln Pike and Walnut Lane (rectory at 2050 East Walnut La.)

locations.label: St. Benedict Church (food pantry and Sunday 8 am Mass)

cost.text: Mass and adoration are free. The FORMED library is covered by the parish. The food pantry page does not mention a fee.

access.notes: The St. Benedict Church food pantry entrance is on the right side of the church and uses a small ramp.

first_step.how: Come to the 10 am Sunday Mass at St. Athanasius, then call the rectory at 215-548-2700 (weekdays 9 am to 4 pm) to ask about ministries or parish updates.
first_step.basis: The site gives a rectory line with weekday hours, a way to get parish updates and a ministries page, and it lists the food pantry and adult groups. It does not describe a welcome program for newcomers.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday Mass is free and open to the public, at 8 am at St. Benedict Church or 10 am at St. Athanasius. The site does not say how long Mass lasts or what happens afterward, so a call to the rectory before your first visit helps. If you come to the food pantry on a Monday or Friday, you sign in, fill out a short self-declaration form, and receive a card for later visits.
first_visit_tips: Arrive early for the food pantry, since the page says some items may be limited.
The pantry does not deliver, so plan to come in person between 10 and 11:30 am on a Monday or Friday.
Sign up for the FORMED library with your name and email; the parish covers the cost.

records.notes: The ministries page lists adoration as 9 am to 6 pm, while the home page and tier 1 say 6:30 pm; 6:30 pm is kept and the difference should be checked by phone. Zoom meeting IDs and passcodes on the ministries page were not recorded. Guiding Star Ministries is listed on that page with a phone number and no meeting details, so it is a lead. The pantry's eligibility rules are not stated on the page. The rectory is the place to ask for Church Cast updates, which the home page says is by phone enrollment. The St. Benedict Church Mass schedule page returned 404, so the Sunday 8 am time comes from the home page.

records.name: St. Augustine Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish near 4th and Vine streets in Old City with Filipino and young adult community groups, Sunday Socials and a History Fair. Its ministries include liturgy, music and outreach.
records.what_you_do: Join the young adult community or the Filipino community, come to Sunday Socials after Mass, or volunteer. Volunteer roles include lectors, communion ministers, music, gardening and cleaning, and food prep and service for the Gift of Life Family House on Sundays and Tuesdays, offsite. Adults who want to become Catholic can join the Becoming Catholic program.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 9 am, 11 am and 7 pm. Weekday Mass at 12:05 pm. Coffee and donuts follow the 9 am and 11 am Masses in the parish hall. The young adult group mostly gathers at the 7 pm Mass.

locations.label: Parish church
locations.address: 4th St., south of Vine St. (rectory at 243 N. Lawrence St.)

cost.text: Mass is free to attend. The socials page does not mention a cost.

access.notes: The church has a wheelchair-accessible entrance by ramp and a wheelchair-accessible restroom. The Rev. Matthew Carr, OSA Parish Hall is also wheelchair accessible.

first_step.how: Come to a Sunday Mass, then download the Registration Form from the parish website and drop it in the Sunday basket or email it to the parish office.
first_step.basis: The site has a registration form, a Becoming Catholic page for adults, and a young adult gathering that invites newcomers to join in. It names the parish phone and email. It does not describe an orientation.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday Mass is free and open to anyone, at 9 am, 11 am or 7 pm. Coffee and donuts follow the 9 am and 11 am Masses in the parish hall. The young adult group is for adults from about 24 into their thirties, mostly gathers at the 7 pm Mass, and invites newcomers to join in with whatever they bring to the conversation.
first_visit_tips: If you want the young adult group, plan on the 7 pm Mass.
Stay after the 9 am or 11 am Mass for coffee and donuts in the parish hall to meet people.
The church has a ramp entrance and an accessible restroom if you use a wheelchair.
Ask the parish office about the 7 pm socials, since the site does not list them.

records.notes: The History Fair on Saturday, October 10, 2026 at Saint Augustine Church is the newest dated item, linked from the home page as a flyer, which is why last_sign_of_life is 2026-10. It is kept out of schedule text. The Filipino Festival of Santo Niño has no date and was not recorded with a time. The young adult page gives no day of the week and no cost. The ministries page gives roles without time or clearance details, so none are recorded. The Councils, Outreach, Liturgy and Music pages were not read. The parish hall on the socials page shares the 243 North Lawrence Street address. The site lists the Gift of Life Family House as a food prep partner, which is a lead.

records.name: St. Barnabas Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish on Buist Avenue in Southwest Philadelphia with Masses in English and a Spanish Mass on Sundays. It also runs religious education and links to a parish school, St. Barnabas Independence Mission School.
records.what_you_do: Come to a weekend Mass, including the Spanish Mass on Sunday at noon. Families can ask about religious education, and the site links to the parish school.

schedule.text: Saturday vigil Mass at 5 pm and a communion service at 8 am. Sunday Masses at 8 am, 10 am and noon, with the noon Mass in Spanish. Weekday Mass at 7 am. Holy days at 9 am and 7 pm. Confessions on Saturdays from 4 to 4:45 pm.

cost.text: Mass is free to attend. The site lists no fee for any activity.

first_step.how: Come to a Sunday Mass (the noon Mass is in Spanish), then call 215-726-1119 or use the parish contact form to ask about religious education or the parish school.
first_step.basis: The site offers an email update sign up and a contact form, but it does not describe a newcomer program or any step for visitors beyond attending Mass.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to the public, in English at most times and in Spanish at noon on Sundays. The site does not describe a welcome step or a family sign up, so the phone call or contact form is the way to ask about religious education.
first_visit_tips: Sunday Masses are at 8 am, 10 am and noon, and the noon Mass is in Spanish.
Call 215-726-1119 or use the contact form to ask about classes for children.
Sign up for the parish email updates on the site if you want news.

records.notes: The Mass schedule page confirmed the Mass times in tier 1. The religious education page and the contact page returned 404, and the home page does not mention religious education, so the religious education line in the summary comes from tier 1 and could not be confirmed on the pages read; it was kept. The only dated items are a June 2019 article about the 100th anniversary and a 2020 footer, which are not evidence of current activity, so status stays probably_active with no last sign of life. The parish school, St. Barnabas Independence Mission School, is linked from the parish site and was dropped from leads: it is a school, not a community group. The home page names no accessibility information, so wheelchair access is not recorded.

records.name: St. Charles Borromeo Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish at 20th and Christian streets in South Philadelphia. It runs a Lectio Divina group, a monthly youth gathering with prayer and a shared meal, and regular adoration and evening prayer.
records.what_you_do: Join the Lectio Divina group at the rectory from 7 to 8 pm, come to adoration from 5 to 6 pm or evening prayer at 5:40 pm (the site does not name the days for these), or come to the youth gathering on the first Sunday of the month at 4:30 pm. The site invites visitors to volunteer through the parish contact page.

schedule.text: Saturday vigil at 8 pm, Sunday Mass at 10:30 am, and weekday Mass at 8:30 am. Confession on weekdays after daily Mass and on Sundays half an hour before Mass. Adoration from 5 to 6 pm and evening prayer at 5:40 pm, with Lectio Divina at the rectory from 7 to 8 pm. The youth gathering is on the first Sunday of each month at 4:30 pm.

locations.label: Parish church and rectory
locations.address: 20th and Christian Sts. (rectory at 902 S. 20th St.)

cost.text: Mass is free to attend. The site does not list a fee for its groups or events.

first_step.how: Come to the Sunday 10:30 am Mass, then email stcharlesborromeo@gmail.com or call 215-735-0600 (weekdays 9 am to 3 pm) to ask about the youth gathering or to volunteer.
first_step.basis: The site gives a parish email, a phone line with office hours and an invitation to volunteer, and it marks the youth gathering as open to all. It does not describe a newcomer welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to the public, with a Saturday vigil at 8 pm and a Sunday Mass at 10:30 am. The Lectio Divina group meets at the rectory at 902 S. 20th Street from 7 to 8 pm, and the site describes it as a Bible reflection session. The first Sunday youth gathering at 4:30 pm includes prayer before the Blessed Sacrament and a shared meal.
first_visit_tips: Call 215-735-0600 on a weekday between 9 am and 3 pm to confirm the day of the week for Lectio Divina, since the site does not give it.
The site gives no parking or transit information, so plan your route before you go.
If you bring a teen, ask about the first Sunday youth gathering, which the site lists for youth from this and nearby parishes.

records.notes: Tier 1 said the weekday Mass was at 8 am; the parish Mass and Confession page says 8:30 am, so 8:30 am is recorded. Tier 1 also called Lectio Divina midweek, but no page read gives the day of the week for Lectio Divina, adoration or evening prayer, so the word was dropped and the day is left for a phone call. One web search did not confirm a day either. The /contact-us and /calendar pages returned 404, and /events showed unrelated placeholder text for another church, so none of those were used. An older archdiocesan list mentions a Hispanic Lectio Divina group at this parish; it is old and unconfirmed, so it was not recorded.

leads_only.name: St. Benedict Church
leads_only.note: Named on the St. Athanasius site as the church at 1940 East Chelten Avenue that hosts its food pantry and an 8 am Sunday Mass. Its own website was not found in the pages read, so it was not checked.

leads_only.name: Guiding Star Ministries
leads_only.note: Listed on the St. Athanasius ministries page with phone 215-924-2876 and no meeting details or website. Not checked.

leads_only.name: Gift of Life Family House
leads_only.note: Named on the St. Augustine volunteer page as a place the parish prepares and serves food for on Sundays and Tuesdays, offsite. Its own website was not found in the pages read, so it was not checked.

notes: One web search (cap 1) was used on the St. Charles Lectio Divina day; it did not confirm the day. 35 page fetches in total, about 3 to 6 per group, with several guessed deep-page URLs returning 404 (listed in the record notes; these were not bot blocks, so blocked is empty). No rate limiting was seen. saschool.org returned a TLS error and was not read. Partner schools named on the sites (St. Athanasius School and St. Barnabas Independence Mission School) were dropped from leads: they are schools, not community groups. The Penn and Drexel Newman small group pages describe the same Newman Center groups that St. Agatha runs, so they were not added as separate leads. Corrections to tier 1: St. Charles weekday Mass is 8:30 am and its Lectio Divina day could not be confirmed, and St. Agatha status moved to active on its 2026 to 2027 OCIA schedule. Budget was not exhausted; searches and fetches stopped once each group's own pages had been read and the open questions were recorded.
